title: Grateful Dead Live at Scranton Catholic Youth Center on 1971-04-13
lineage: SBD > MR > DAT > FLAC > DAW(Bertha) > Audio DVD > DVD Audio Extractor v.3.3.2 (audio files extracted prior to burning to DVD disc) > 24/48 wav > downsampled to 44.1 wav with Wave Lab v.5.00a > dithered to from 24-16 bit depth with Wave Lab UV22 HR Plugin > SBEs fixed with shntool v.2.0.3 (by set) > files rennamed with File Renamer v.1.0.0 > FLAC encoding with FLAC Frontend v.1.7.1 Etree Edition, FLAC v.1.1.2 (level 6)
source: Bertha Remaster of the Master Reel source (shn ID 32015)

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1971 show with smoking Good Lovin', Second That Emotion, Sugar Magnolia and Hard to Handle, despite minor clipping.
ai_review.review: The remastered soundboard delivers surprising depth and clarity, letting listeners feel the band’s massive presence even though a few song starts/ends are clipped and there is a hint of high‑end peaking. Musically the show bursts with energy – first‑set classics dance‑ready, a wacky groove on Hard to Handle, a raging Sugar Magnolia, hypnotic Truckin', and a monster Good Lovin' jam that rolls into Second That Emotion before a sweet Uncle John’s Band closer. Overall the performance is praised as “outrageous” and “supernova‑level,” with only minor recording quirks noted.

ai_rating.rationale: Multiple 5‑star reviews highlight exceptional musical moments and a high‑quality soundboard, with only occasional technical glitches; the weighted average of show (70%) and recording (30%) yields a rating in the top tier.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Remastered depth and clarity, overall crisp mix; minor issues include clipped beginnings/endings of five songs and slight high‑end peaking noted by one listener.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Energetic first set with peppy, dance‑ready versions; second set builds into extended jams (Good Lovin' → Darkness jam → Second That Emotion) and finishes with a sweet Uncle John’s Band, despite a curfew truncation.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Guitar described as glistening, shredding, off the charts throughout; his tone praised heavily.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass “sits in your lap”; even takes lead vocal duties at the start of Cumberland Blues.
band_member_comments.Bob: Strong vocal presence; front‑stage banter with a British spot‑light guy; sings on Casey Jones and other numbers.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ is missed by one reviewer but his vocals are highlighted as “on fire” during Good Lovin' and other jams.
